recipes.name: Peach Pound Cake
ingredients_raw: 2 cups fresh peaches, pitted and chopped

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Butter a 10-inch tube pan and dust with white sugar.
Beat sugar and butter together in a mixing bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy; add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in vanilla.
Sift 2 ¾ cups flour, baking powder, and salt together into a bowl; gradually stir flour mixture into butter mixture.
Place remaining 1/4 cup flour into a small bowl. Add peaches and toss to coat, then fold floured peaches into batter. Spread batter evenly into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 60 to 70 minutes. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Peach Pound Cake
raw_recipe.description: This buttery peach pound cake is easy to make with fresh, juicy peaches and easy baking ingredients for a delicious and welcome summer treat.

video.description: In this video we show you how to make a pound cake that is filled with sweet juicy peaches. The cake uses ingredients you probably already have in your pantry and is simple to make. It bakes in about an hour, so dessert is never too far away.

review.reviewBody: Half of this recipe was just perfect in an 8x4" loaf pan. I lowered the heat to 325 degrees after some reviewers indicated they had trouble getting the cake to bake through without overbaking the exterior. It was perfect, then, at 325 for about 60 minutes. I made this exactly as written, in spite of reviewer suggestions to add this or that. I didn't want to take away from the buttery, peachy taste--it was delicious. The sugar crust is a nice touch and I'm glad I included that too. I used frozen peaches, thawed and drained, and drizzled the baked loaf with a glaze of powdered sugar and the drained peach juice. Very pretty, moist cake, with a just right taste and speckle of peaches.

Good recipe! I added a carmel glaze that made it even more delicious: 1/2 c. butter - 1/2 c. packed brown sugar - 2 tsp. milk - Heat all ingred. in saucepan, stir occasionally. Boil 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Spoon over warm cake. I will use this recipe for a pineapple pound cake next, using drained canned pineapple. Thanks!

Great recipe! I use fresh peaches. I made a glaze. 1 cup of powdered sugar; 2 Tablespoons of water; 1/8 teaspoon of LorAnn Peach extract. Whisk and put in sandwich bag, cut small amount from corner and the drizzle.

I’m giving this 5 stars because it’s absolutely foolproof. I didn’t have the Bundt pan so used a 9x13. No problem. I chopped up a large, drained can of peaches and folded them into the batter. Also no problem. I sprinkled sugar on the bottom of the greased pan thinking I would have a burnt mess. Nope. Came out perfectly moist and peachy with a slightly crust. Delicious!

This is delicious!!!! I made it as directed the first time and took to a BBQ as a dessert and everyone loved it. I made it again, cutting the recipe in half for the cake portion, in a shallow baking dish and topped with Italian prune plums and some sugar. WOW

Easy delicious recipe. I added a few tbs of sour cream. I mixed the butter and sugar & then batter a little longer which helped make the cake rise better. Also I had a few peaches left so next time I would add more. Yummy!

I prepared it exactly like the recipe, but added an amaretto glaze. I used fresh peaches that were very rioe. Also added cinnamon and nutmeg, and sprinkled the interior of the pan with turbinado sugar before adding the batter. I baked the cake 10-15 mins longer than recipe suggested. Perfect! Turbinado sugar added a nice crunch.
I halved the recipe and made it in a loaf pan. Put only 3/4 cup of sugar and it was still sweet enough! Buttery and rich enough! The coat of sugar in the pan is a nice touch!

I love this cake. I did increase the peaches . To be honest I didn't even measure them but I used 5 good size peaches and added a little cinnamon and nutmeg to the dry ingredients. It did take longer to bake, about an extra 1o minutes but I did not decrease the temp. It turned out perfect. FYI: We live at 4000ft.

Delicious! I tried the recipe with cherries. I used 2 cups of pitted chopped fresh cherries and the one difference was I used cake flour instead of all purpose and I did not sugar the pans. Everybody who tried it loved it. Thanks for the great recipe.

I'm at high altitude so a adjusted for that, bit less baking powder, 4 xl eggs, juicy fresh peaches peeled and diced and a tad more flour. I baked at 330 for 45 min, then 325 for 20 more min. came out perfect! glazed with peach juice, mixed with vanilla and powdered sugar.

This cake is delicious! I chopped fresh peaches small dice, could possibly add 3 cups next time . I peeled the peaches but you probably don’t have too? I cut the Bundt cake into 4 chunks and wrap and freeze. The sugar coated pan makes a huge difference so don’t skip it! So yummy 😋
We loved it! Will definitely be making it again.
Added an extra egg only.

When you put it in 1/2, the instructions still tell you to divide 2 3/4 of the flour when you're actually only using 1 1/2 cups of flour. I had to ad 1/2 cup of sour cream because the batter was so thick.
My husband adores this cake. Just picked up the last of this summer’s Michigan peaches and will bake and freeze to enjoy into Fall.

Not exaggerating: my mother, the most stoic woman I've ever met in my life, cried upon taking her first bite of this. Dent norton, I commend you. This cake was absolutely lovely and the whole family enjoyed it. Thank you.
Moist and very flavorful! A great way to use some of my fresh peaches I get every year about this time.

I like the recipe. I did make a couple of changes. I used jar peaches because I had them on hand. I also added some cinnamon to the batter and sprinkled the cake pan with butter and cinnamon sugar. I did add about 2 tablespoons of the juice from the peaches and a tablespoon of sour cream for moisture because that was all I had. I think over all its a good recipe. I would like it a little sweeter but it was moist. The next time I may use half white sugar and half brown sugar. I will also use brown sugar in the pan like you would for a pineapple upside down cake. I will add a little more extract for flavor. I have to try fresh peaches that may add to the flavor too. I did make a light glaze to pour on top. Not too sweet. Great recipe!
It's in the oven now. I did not use sugar. Diabetic. I used condensed milk 1/2 can and juice from peaches (not syrup). Only 60 calories. I will revisit review after finishing cooking.
